also: there is no time to waste

terms.gloss: time: the time that passes, and the time for something
evidence: Cic. Att. 13.45.2: ad tempus redīre, to come back in time (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: English “time” is several Latin words: free time is ōtium (see leisure, spare time), an age or period aetās (see age), the time of day hōra (see hour, what time is it?), an occasion tempus or aliās (see occasion), and “three times” a numeral adverb, ter. In the ablative, tempore alone means “in time, gradually”, and temperī “on time”.

phrases.latin: tempore rūricolae patiēns fit taurus arātrī
phrases.english: in time the bull comes to bear the farmer’s plough

phrases.source: Plin. Ep. 6.31.17 (Lewis & Short s.v. prōcēdō); Traupman 394

phrases.english: there is no time to waste (literally “there is need of haste”)
phrases.source: Traupman 395; cf. Liv. 24.23: quam mātūrātō opus erat (Lewis & Short s.v. mātūrō)

phrases.latin: ōtium nōn habēre (+ dative of the gerund)
phrases.english: not to have the time to (do something)

sources: John C. Traupman, Conversational Latin for Oral Proficiency, pp. 394, 395.
